LESSON: LINES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry
Topic 3.1: Lines
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Lines, part of Geometry in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why are perpendicular lines significant in our day to day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Work with peers to identify lines in the classroom and within the environment. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication (AAC) to perform the task.

2. Describe in purposive pairs/groups lines in the environment and identify them as horizontal and vertical lines, parallel and perpendicular lines.

3. Work with purposive peers to draw/trace/stamp and model horizontal and vertical lines, parallel and perpendicular lines. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Work with peers to identify lines in the classroom and within the environment. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication (AAC) to perform the task.
2. Describe in purposive pairs/groups lines in the environment and identify them as horizontal and vertical lines, parallel and perpendicular lines.
3. Work with purposive peers to draw/trace/stamp and model horizontal and vertical lines, parallel and perpendicular lines. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Lines together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: as the learner works with peers to draw and model horizontal and vertical lines, parallel and perpendicular line.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: as the learner shows environmental awareness as they team up with peers to identify lines in the

classroom and within the environment.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate line to sketching and drawing in Creative Arts.
